content: The following references provide detailed insights into various aspects of infection control, respiratory disease management, and healthcare practices: 1. Rosenthal et al. (2000) studied the impact of education and performance feedback on handwashing practices in Argentinean hospitals, emphasizing the role of administrative support in improving compliance. 2. Pang et al. 3. Chen et al. (2006) analyzed the epidemiology and control strategies of the SARS outbreak at Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore, providing valuable lessons for future outbreaks. 4. Lau et al. 5. Yassi et al. (2004) explored knowledge gaps and research priorities for protecting healthcare workers from occupationally acquired respiratory infections. 6. Imai et al. (2005) examined healthcare workers' perceptions of SARS risk in Japan, emphasizing the need for effective communication and training. 7. Ho et al. (2003) discussed hospital infection control and admission strategies during the SARS outbreak, focusing on minimizing nosocomial transmission. 8. The CDC (2004) provided guidelines on respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette in healthcare settings to prevent the spread of respiratory infections. 9. Castro et al. (1990) outlined tuberculosis transmission prevention strategies in healthcare settings, with a focus on HIV-related issues. 10. Puro et al. (2006) reported on clustered pneumonia cases among healthcare workers in Italian hospitals, applying WHO SARS alert protocols. 11. 12. Garner (1996) developed guidelines for isolation precautions in hospitals to prevent the spread of infectious diseases. 13. Olsen et al. (2005) documented family clustering of avian influenza A (H5N1) cases, underscoring the need for vigilance in outbreak settings. 14. Lai et al. (2005) studied the survival of the SARS coronavirus, providing insights into its environmental stability and implications for infection control. 15. Luby et al. (2005) conducted a randomized controlled trial on the effect of handwashing on child health, demonstrating significant health benefits. 16. Hammond et al. (2000) evaluated the impact of hand sanitizer use on absenteeism in elementary schools, showing a reduction in illness-related absences. 17. Gopalakrishna et al. 18. Reynolds et al. (2006) identified factors associated with nosocomial SARS-CoV transmission among healthcare workers in Hanoi, Vietnam. 19. Fowler et al. 20. Scales et al. 21. Douglas (1975) discussed the role of nosocomial influenza infections in causing intercurrent fevers in infants, highlighting the need for infection control. 22. Chan et al. (2004) focused on the detection of SARS coronavirus in suspected cases, emphasizing the importance of accurate diagnostic methods. 23. Bloomfield (2003) proposed a risk-based approach to home hygiene, addressing the prevention of infectious diseases in household settings. 24. Rheinbaben et al. (2000) studied virus transmission via contact in household settings, using bacteriophage as a model virus. 25. 26. Chemaly et al. (2006) conducted a retrospective study on respiratory viral infections in adults with hematologic malignancies and stem cell transplant recipients. 27. Kallander et al. (2005) evaluated home and community management of acute respiratory infections in children across eight Ugandan districts. 28. Richards et al. (2005) conducted a randomized controlled trial on home management of community-acquired pneumonia, demonstrating its feasibility. 29. Quinlan et al. (2003) explored restrictive visitor policies in healthcare settings, gathering feedback from healthcare workers, patients, and families. 30. Lee et al. (2004) reviewed infection control practices for SARS in Laos, Taiwan, and Thailand, based on experiences from mobile containment teams. 31. Mukhopadhyay et al. (2004) reported on a SARS case involving a hospital visitor and her intensivist, highlighting the risks of nosocomial transmission. 32. Melnyk et al. (2004) evaluated a program aimed at empowering parents of critically ill children, showing positive effects on mental health and coping outcomes. 33. Saunders et al. (2003) assessed practices for improving family-centered care in neonatal intensive care units, identifying areas for improvement. 34. Griffin (2006) emphasized the importance of family-centered care in neonatal intensive care units, advocating for better communication and support. 35. Chaovavanich et al. (2004) documented early containment efforts for SARS at Bamrasnaradura Institute in Thailand, providing a model for outbreak response. 36. Svoboda et al. 37. Lim et al. 38. Dey et al. (2001) conducted a randomized controlled trial to promote influenza vaccination uptake among healthcare workers, showing improved vaccination rates. 39. Lester et al. (2003) examined the use, effectiveness, and attitudes toward influenza vaccines among house staff, identifying barriers to vaccination. 40. Davis et al. (2006) highlighted the role of influenza vaccination as secondary prevention for cardiovascular disease, based on recommendations from the American Heart Association. 41. Cox et al. 42. Lloyd-Smith et al. (2003) analyzed strategies to curtail SARS transmission within communities and hospitals, providing insights into effective interventions. 43. Tsai et al. (2004) assessed the impact of a SARS outbreak on a hospital in Taiwan, highlighting the challenges of outbreak management. 44. Riley et al. (1978) investigated airborne measles transmission in a suburban elementary school, demonstrating the importance of ventilation in infection control. 45. Green-McKenzie et al. (2001) evaluated infection control practices among correctional healthcare workers, identifying the influence of management attitudes and equipment availability. 46. Moore et al. (2005) explored factors affecting adherence to infection control guidelines among healthcare workers during the SARS outbreak. 47. Ofner et al. 48. Seto et al. (2003) demonstrated the effectiveness of droplet and contact precautions in preventing nosocomial SARS transmission. 49. Chia et al. (2005) reviewed the appropriate use of personal protective equipment among healthcare workers during the SARS outbreak in Singapore. 50. Rengasamy et al. (2004) conducted a literature review on respiratory protection against bioaerosols, identifying research needs for healthcare settings. These studies collectively provide a comprehensive understanding of infection prevention, outbreak management, and healthcare worker safety in various settings.
